questions.question: What are the main components that make up a basic pinhole camera?
options: A closed, empty box with a small hole on the front face and a screen on the back face
A glass tube filled with gas, with electrodes at both ends
A set of curved mirrors mounted inside a solid plastic cylinder
A dual-lens system inside a tube with a digital sensor at the front

questions.question: How does light travel from a source through a pinhole camera to form an image?
options: It travels in curved paths around the edges of the box
It moves in straight lines from the source, through the pinhole, to the back screen
It bounces back and forth inside the box until it hits the front face again
It is refracted by the air inside the box to focus onto a central point

questions.question: If you poke several additional small holes near the original pinhole of a pinhole camera, what is the result?
options: A single, extremely sharp and bright image is formed
No image can be seen at all because the light rays cancel out
Multiple images are produced on the screen
The image becomes completely upside down and magnified

questions.question: What happens to the image on a pinhole camera's screen if the pinhole is made significantly larger?
options: The image becomes sharper but much dimmer
The image becomes brighter but blurred
The image disappears and only a single dot is visible
The image becomes inverted and smaller

questions.question: What occurs when some of the light from an object passes through a lens and is focused on a screen?
options: An image is formed on the screen
The light is completely absorbed and turned into heat
The light is split into a double shadow with no image
A virtual image is created that can only be seen inside the lens itself

questions.question: How does a convex lens affect light rays, and what is the term for the point where these rays meet?
options: It refracts rays so they travel more towards each other, meeting at a focus
It reflects rays away from each other, meeting at a normal
It absorbs all rays, meeting at a shadow point
It disperses rays into a spectrum, meeting at a boundary

questions.question: How does the refraction of light vary across the shape of a converging lens?
options: Light is refracted more near the centre than at the edges
Light is refracted equally at all points across the lens
Light is refracted more at the edges than near the centre
Light is only refracted at the exact centre of the lens

questions.question: Which of the following describes the size, orientation, and distance of a reflection in a plane mirror?
options: Same size, upright, and the same distance behind the mirror as the object is in front
Larger size, inverted, and closer to the mirror than the object is in front
Smaller size, upright, and twice as far behind the mirror as the object is in front
Same size, inverted, and half the distance behind the mirror as the object is in front

questions.question: What type of inversion is observed in a plane mirror reflection when an object is facing us?
options: Vertical inversion, where the top and bottom are swapped
Lateral inversion, where the left and right sides appear swapped
No inversion at all; it is a perfect copy
Radial inversion, where the center and edges are swapped

questions.question: Why are reflections in a mirror classified as virtual images?
options: Because they appear where light rays seem to have come from, not where they actually come from
Because they can be projected onto a paper screen held behind the mirror
Because they are formed by physical light rays physically crossing behind the glass
Because they only exist when viewed through an electronic sensor

questions.question: What determines the colour of an object when it is illuminated by white or coloured light?
options: The speed of light reflecting off its surface
The amounts of red, green, and blue light it is reflecting
The total thickness of the object's surface layer
The angle at which the light hits the object's surface

questions.question: Why does a white object appear red when illuminated by red light?
options: Because white objects absorb red light and emit green light
Because white objects reflect all colours of light, so they look the same colour as the incident light
Because red light changes the chemical composition of the white surface
Because white objects only reflect red light and absorb all other colours of the spectrum

questions.question: What happens to the colours of light that an object does not reflect, and how does this explain black objects?
options: They are refracted; black objects refract all colours of light
They are scattered; black objects scatter all colours of light in different directions
They are absorbed; black objects absorb all colours of light
They are transmitted; black objects let all colours of light pass through them

questions.question: When light enters a transparent material from air, what direction does it turn relative to the normal?
options: It turns towards the normal
It turns away from the normal
It continues in a straight line without turning
It reflects directly back along the normal

questions.question: When light leaves a transparent material and re-enters the air, what path does it take?
options: It turns towards the normal
It turns away from the normal
It continues parallel to the normal
It stops and is completely absorbed by the boundary

questions.question: What is created when you mix equal amounts of two primary colours of light, and what is created when you mix all three primary colours in equal amounts?
options: A secondary colour is created; all three mixed makes white
A tertiary colour is created; all three mixed makes black
A darker shade is created; all three mixed makes grey
A primary colour is created; all three mixed makes a rainbow spectrum
